## Solution

We evaluate
$$I = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{|z|=1} \frac{6z^{98}}{23z^{99}-2z^{81}+z^4-7}\,dz$$
by the residue theorem. Let $P(z)=23z^{99}-2z^{81}+z^4-7$ and $f(z)=\frac{6z^{98}}{P(z)}$.

**Step 1: Locate the poles.** The poles of $f$ are the zeros of $P$. We apply Rouché's theorem on $|z|=1$. Write $P(z)=\underbrace{23z^{99}}_{g(z)}+\underbrace{(-2z^{81}+z^4-7)}_{h(z)}$. On $|z|=1$:
$$|g(z)|=23, \qquad |h(z)|\le 2+1+7=10<23=|g(z)|.$$
By Rouché, $P$ and $g$ have the same number of zeros inside $|z|=1$, namely $99$. Since $\deg P=99$, **all** $99$ zeros of $P$ lie inside the unit disk. Also $P(0)=-7\neq 0$, so $z=0$ is not a pole.

**Step 2: Use the residue at infinity.** The sum of all residues in the extended plane is $0$:
$$\sum_{\text{finite poles}}\operatorname{Res}(f,z_k)=-\operatorname{Res}(f,\infty).$$
Since every finite pole lies inside $|z|=1$, the integral equals the sum of all finite residues, i.e. $I=-\operatorname{Res}(f,\infty)$.

**Step 3: Compute $\operatorname{Res}(f,\infty)$.** Set $z=1/w$:
$$f(1/w)=\frac{6w^{-98}}{23w^{-99}-2w^{-81}+w^{-4}-7}=\frac{6w^{-98}}{w^{-99}(23-2w^{18}+w^{95}-7w^{99})}=\frac{6w}{23-2w^{18}+w^{95}-7w^{99}}.$$
Then
$$\frac{f(1/w)}{w^2}=\frac{6}{w\,(23-2w^{18}+w^{95}-7w^{99})}.$$
Near $w=0$ the denominator factor $(23-2w^{18}+w^{95}-7w^{99})\to 23$, so
$$\operatorname{Res}\!\left(\frac{f(1/w)}{w^2},\,0\right)=\frac{6}{23}.$$
Hence $\operatorname{Res}(f,\infty)=-\frac{6}{23}$.

**Step 4: Conclude.**
$$I=-\operatorname{Res}(f,\infty)=\frac{6}{23}.$$

$$\boxed{\dfrac{6}{23}}$$
